newsitem.title: USA: US rail intermodal, carloads up from yr ago - AAR.
newsitem.headline: US rail intermodal, carloads up from yr ago - AAR.

text.p: U.S. rail freight traffic as measured in intermodal rose 38.4 percent in the week ended Nov 23 from the same 1995 week, which included the Thanksgiving holiday, Association of American Railroads said Wednesday.
AAR said that intermodal traffic, which does not include carloads, totaled 170,182 trailers and containers in the week versus 122,957 in the year-ago week.
Carloads also rose 22 percent to 357,277 in the week from 292,742 a year ago.
Ton-miles increased 24.7 percent to 26.8 billion from 21.5 billion a year ago. A ton-mile, a measure of freight transportation, equates one ton of freight hauled one mile.

AAR said carloads of metallic ores fell 1.3 percent to 17,445 in the November 23 week from 17,675 in the year-ago week. But it said all other major commodity groups reported had increases from a year ago.
Grain loadings rose 23.1 percent to 26,440 carloads in the week from 21,481 last year, while lumber and wood products increased 34.5 percent to 5,168 carloads from 3,841, AAR said.
Petroleum loadings, at 5,483 in the week, were up 38.4 percent from 3,963 last year. AAR also said that carloads of coal increased 18.6 percent to 138,253 from 116,523 a year ago.
Motor vehicles and equipment increased 52 percent to 22,599 carloads last week from 14,863 in the same 1995 week.

Grain mill products were up 19.4 percent to 10,073 carloads in the week from 8,433 in the year-ago week, while farm products other than grain rose 3.6 percent to 2,359 carloads from 2,278 in the same 1995 week, it said.
In the first 47 weeks of 1996, AAR said ton-miles rose 2.4 percent from the same period last year. Intermodal traffic also rose 2.2 percent, but carloads fell 0.2 percent, AAR said.
